YMCA FRENCH DAY CAMPS 


HURDLE LANGUAGE BARRIERS 
SUBJECT/ SUJET

PecouUMOUER AVES 
COMMUNIQUER 
CONTACT WILLIAM SHER 


Westmount YMCA is preparing to open another breach in the 
artificial barriers which sometimes stigmatize its community 


as a bastion of English-speaking insularity. 


In doing so, it will also re-test the spreading convinction 
that children can best be motivated to learn when they are 


enjoying themselves in a relaxed environment. 


Following last year's example by the International YMCA in 
Montreal's Mile End district, Westmount Branch will this 


summer operate a French-language day camp. 


But there are some significant differences in the objectives 


of the two camps. 


Targets of International Y's program, to be expanded this year, 
are children of immigrants who speak their parents' native 


language and have mastered English. 


Operating much like any other day camp--but in French only-- 
it will again use the pool, the gym, arts and crafts, music, 
magazines and movies to motivate the youngsters to learn a 
third language so they can participate fully in the activities 


of their choice. 


Unlike school, where children are often indifferent to or resent 
having to study another language, last year's pilot project at 


International Y showed they came to consider French as the key to 


an enjoyable exciting experience. 
Westmount Y's camp will operate along similar lines--but for 
children whose native tongue is English. In addition to 


whetting their desire to learn French as a living Language, 


it will also attempt to arouse their interest in French culture.
